parts.prompt: An annular sector has inner radius $r$, outer radius $2r$ and area $A$. Express its complete perimeter in terms of $r$ and $A$ only.

A chord $AB$ of a circle of radius $r$ subtends an angle $2\theta$ at the centre $O$, where $0<\theta<\pi/2$. Show that the perimeter of the minor segment bounded by chord $AB$ and the minor arc $AB$ is $2r(\theta+\sin\theta)$.

figure.purpose: Make the exact symbolic region and boundary in the stem unambiguous.
figure.alt_text: A not-to-scale diagram of circle with centre O, radii OA and OB, minor chord AB and minor arc AB; it shows the given labels but no derived result.
figure.brief: Objects: circle with centre O, radii OA and OB, minor chord AB and minor arc AB. Orientation: place O below the horizontal chord AB, with A left and B right. Required labels and marks: label OA=OB=r and the central angle AOB=2 theta. Omit: no perpendicular bisector or half-angle construction, chord formula, arc length, perimeter expression, working or answer. Use a clean, answer-safe, not-to-scale teacher sketch.

parts.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $AB=AC=2r$ and $\angle BAC=2\theta$, where $0<\theta\leq\pi/3$. A sector with centre $A$, radius $r$ and angle $2\theta$ lies inside the triangle. Express the area of the part of the triangle outside the sector in terms of $r$ and $\theta$.

figure.purpose: Make the exact symbolic region and boundary in the stem unambiguous.
figure.alt_text: A not-to-scale diagram of isosceles triangle ABC with AB=AC and a smaller sector centred at A entirely inside the triangle; it shows the given labels but no derived result.
figure.brief: Objects: isosceles triangle ABC with AB=AC and a smaller sector centred at A entirely inside the triangle. Orientation: place A at the top and BC as a horizontal base; draw the sector between sides AB and AC near A. Required labels and marks: label AB=AC=2r, sector radii r, and angle BAC=2 theta; shade the triangle outside the inner sector. Omit: no area formulas, derived expressions, working or answer. Use a clean, answer-safe, not-to-scale teacher sketch.

parts.prompt: In a circle of radius $r$, chord $AB$ subtends angle $2\alpha$ at the centre, where $0<\alpha<\pi/2$. Express the area of the major segment bounded by chord $AB$ and the major arc in terms of $r$ and $\alpha$, simplifying with a double-angle identity.

figure.purpose: Make the exact symbolic region and boundary in the stem unambiguous.
figure.alt_text: A not-to-scale diagram of complete circle with centre O, radii OA and OB, chord AB, minor arc AB and major arc AB; it shows the given labels but no derived result.
figure.brief: Objects: complete circle with centre O, radii OA and OB, chord AB, minor arc AB and major arc AB. Orientation: place chord AB vertically to the right of O, with A above and B below. Required labels and marks: label OA=OB=r and angle AOB=2 alpha; shade the major segment on the side of chord AB containing O and the major arc. Omit: no minor-segment formula, circle subtraction, identity, working or answer. Use a clean, answer-safe, not-to-scale teacher sketch.

parts.prompt: Square $ABCD$ has side length $2r$. A quarter-circle arc from $B$ to $D$ is centred at $A$. Find, in exact form, the area of the circular segment bounded by chord $BD$ and the quarter-circle arc $BD$.

figure.purpose: Make the exact symbolic region and boundary in the stem unambiguous.
figure.alt_text: A not-to-scale diagram of square ABCD and a quarter-circle arc BD centred at vertex A, with chord BD drawn as the square diagonal; it shows the given labels but no derived result.
figure.brief: Objects: square ABCD and a quarter-circle arc BD centred at vertex A, with chord BD drawn as the square diagonal. Orientation: place A bottom left, B bottom right, C top right and D top left; draw the quarter-circle arc from B to D inside the square. Required labels and marks: label AB=AD=2r; shade only the region between chord BD and arc BD. Omit: no sector area, triangle area, working or answer. Use a clean, answer-safe, not-to-scale teacher sketch.

parts.prompt: Tangents from $T$ touch a circle of radius $r$ at $A$ and $B$. The angle $AOB$ at the centre is $2\theta$, where $0<\theta<\pi/2$, and $T$ lies outside the minor sector $OAB$. Show that the area enclosed by $TA$, $TB$ and the minor arc $AB$ is $r^2(\tan\theta-\theta)$.

figure.purpose: Make the exact symbolic region and boundary in the stem unambiguous.
figure.alt_text: A not-to-scale diagram of circle centre O, tangency points A and B, external point T, radii OA and OB, tangents TA and TB, and line OT; it shows the given labels but no derived result.
figure.brief: Objects: circle centre O, tangency points A and B, external point T, radii OA and OB, tangents TA and TB, and line OT. Orientation: place O left and T right, with A upper right and B lower right on the circle; show the minor arc AB facing T. Required labels and marks: label OA=OB=r and angle AOB=2 theta; mark right angles OAT and OBT and equal tangents TA and TB; shade the region bounded by TA, TB and minor arc AB. Omit: no tangent length, kite area, sector area, working or target derivation. Use a clean, answer-safe, not-to-scale teacher sketch.

parts.prompt: An annular sector has inner radius $r$, outer radius $R$, angle $\theta$ and area $A$, where $R>r>0$ and $0<\theta<2\pi$. Eliminate $R$ and express its complete perimeter in terms of $A$, $r$ and $\theta$ only.

figure.purpose: Make the exact symbolic region and boundary in the stem unambiguous.
figure.alt_text: A not-to-scale diagram of annular sector with common centre O, outer radius R, inner radius r, two concentric arcs and two radial edges; it shows the given labels but no derived result.
figure.brief: Objects: annular sector with common centre O, outer radius R, inner radius r, two concentric arcs and two radial edges. Orientation: draw a wedge opening to the right with the smaller sector removed from the same centre. Required labels and marks: label the outer radius R, inner radius r, central angle theta, and region area A. Omit: no perimeter formula, rearrangement for R, working or answer. Use a clean, answer-safe, not-to-scale teacher sketch.
